activity.notes: John A. Macdonald served as the first Prime Minister of Canada from Confederation on 1 July 1867 until 5 November 1873. His later return to the same office in 1878 followed a genuine interruption in office, so ATLAS models the two premierships as separate Activities rather than one continuous term.

sources.title: National Program for the Grave Sites of Canadian Prime Ministers
sources.citation_text: Parks Canada lists the Right Honourable Sir John Alexander Macdonald as Prime Minister from 1 July 1867 to 5 November 1873 and again from 17 October 1878 to 6 June 1891.

sources.title: First Ministry - Guide to Canadian Ministries since Confederation
sources.citation_text: The Government of Canada's Guide to Canadian Ministries identifies the First Ministry as 1 July 1867 to 5 November 1873 and names Sir John Alexander Macdonald as Prime Minister.

sources.title: MACDONALD, Sir JOHN ALEXANDER
sources.citation_text: The Dictionary of Canadian Biography documents Macdonald's pre-Confederation political leadership and his central role in Confederation, providing scholarly biographical context for his selection as Canada's first prime minister.
